chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Yunus ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ya'qub Ishaq ibn Abdullah from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said:
Allah, Blessed and Exalted, reproached His servants with two verses from His Book: to not speak until they know, and to not reject what they do not know.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Was a covenant not taken from them in the Book that they would not say anything about Allah except the truth?' [7:169]
And He says: 'In fact, they rejected the Book without comprehending it and before the fulfilment of its warnings.' [10:39]

key_terms.تَأْوِيلُهُ: Fulfilment/interpretation — the ultimate realization or authoritative explanation of a text
key_terms.عَيَّرَ: Reproached, rebuked — a strong term indicating divine disapproval directed at a specific failing
key_terms.مِيثَاقُ الْكِتَابِ: The covenant of the Book — the binding obligation derived from Scripture

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about speaking without knowledge in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that Allah has warned His servants through two Quranic verses against two intellectual vices: speaking about what one does not know, and rejecting what one has not understood. This hadith, transmitted through the chain of the Saduq family and the reliable narrator Ibn Abi Umayr, underscores that both rash speech and hasty rejection stem from ignorance. The original audience — scholars and students of the early Shia community — would have understood this as a call for epistemic humility and rigorous adherence to knowledge before speaking or dismissing.
